plants_chloroplast_0001.location: Main Structures: chloroplasts and thylakoid membranes
plants_chloroplast_0001.claim: In which plant-cell organelle does photosynthesis take place? Answer: Chloroplast. Chlorophyll in thylakoid membranes absorbs light. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

plants_cactus_spines_0001.location: Figure 30.35(a): modified leaves and photosynthetic stem
plants_cactus_spines_0001.claim: Which organs became spines in the prickly pear cactus? Answer: Leaves. This shape reduces water loss; photosynthesis takes place in green stems.

plants_coast_redwood_0001.claim: Which species is known for the tallest living trees? Answer: Coast redwood. The species is Sequoia sempervirens; height is distinct from trunk volume. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

plants_flytrap_leaves_0001.location: Venus flytraps: modified trap leaves; trigger hairs; lobes of a leaf
plants_flytrap_leaves_0001.claim: Which organ of a Venus flytrap forms its snapping trap? Answer: Leaf. Sensitive hairs inside the trap respond to contact with prey.

plants_guard_cells_0001.location: Control of Transpiration: two guard cells surrounding stomata
plants_guard_cells_0001.claim: Which cells regulate the opening and closing of a leaf stoma? Answer: Guard cells. By changing shape, a pair of these cells regulates gas exchange and water-vapor loss. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

plants_transpiration_0001.location: Movement of Water and Minerals in the Xylem: transpiration
plants_transpiration_0001.claim: What is the loss of water from a plant as vapor called? Answer: Transpiration. Evaporation at leaf surfaces helps create tension in the xylem. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

plants_negative_gravitropism_0001.location: Plant Responses to Gravity: upward shoot growth
plants_negative_gravitropism_0001.claim: What is shoot growth against the direction of gravity called? Answer: Negative gravitropism. The response to gravity differs from phototropism, a response to light direction. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

plants_ethylene_0001.location: Ethylene: volatile hormone; paper bag and neighboring fruit
plants_ethylene_0001.claim: Which gaseous plant hormone promotes fruit ripening? Answer: Ethylene. Gas released by one ripening fruit can accelerate the ripening of nearby fruit.

plants_phytochrome_0001.location: The Phytochrome System: red/far-red photointerconvertible forms
plants_phytochrome_0001.claim: Which plant photoreceptor switches between Pr and Pfr forms? Answer: Phytochrome. The forms differ in their absorption of red and far-red light. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

plants_oxygen_source_0001.location: Photosystem II: water splitting and diatomic oxygen
plants_oxygen_source_0001.claim: Which substance supplies the O₂ released by a plant during photosynthesis? Answer: Water (H₂O). Water is split in the light reactions; two water molecules supply one O₂ molecule. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

human_body_iris_0001.location: Iris: colored part controlling pupil size
human_body_iris_0001.claim: What is the colored part of the eye surrounding the pupil called? Answer: Iris. It changes pupil size and helps regulate how much light enters the eye. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

human_body_paired_kidneys_0001.location: Opening: two bean-shaped organs, one on each side of spine
human_body_paired_kidneys_0001.claim: Which of these organs is paired in typical human anatomy? Answer: Kidney. Two kidneys lie on opposite sides of the spine and filter blood. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

human_body_bladder_0001.location: Opening: ureters carry urine to bladder for storage
human_body_bladder_0001.claim: In which organ is urine stored before leaving the body? Answer: Urinary bladder. Urine reaches this organ from the kidneys through the ureters.

human_body_heart_chambers_0001.location: Heart chambers: two atria and two ventricles
human_body_heart_chambers_0001.claim: How many chambers does a normal human heart have? Answer: 4. The two upper chambers are atria and the two lower chambers are ventricles.

human_body_alveoli_0001.location: Air fills your lung’s air sacs; Oxygen flows into your blood
human_body_alveoli_0001.claim: What are the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange occurs called? Answer: Alveoli. Across their walls, oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide moves from blood into air. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

human_body_cochlea_0001.location: Steps 3–4: snail-shaped cochlea, fluid and hair cells
human_body_cochlea_0001.claim: Which fluid-filled structure in the inner ear has a spiral shape? Answer: Cochlea. It contains sensory hair cells that help detect sound.

human_body_bile_producer_0001.location: How does my digestive system break food into small parts? Liver and Gallbladder
human_body_bile_producer_0001.claim: Which organ produces bile? Answer: Liver. The gallbladder stores it; bile helps digest fats.

human_body_olfactory_location_0001.location: How does your sense of smell work? Small patch high inside nose
human_body_olfactory_location_0001.claim: Where are the sensory neurons that detect odors located? Answer: High inside the nasal cavity. Odor molecules stimulate their receptors, and signals then travel to the brain.

human_body_ileum_0001.location: What is the digestive system? Three parts of small intestine versus large intestine
human_body_ileum_0001.claim: Which of these structures is part of the small intestine? Answer: Ileum. It is the final section, following the duodenum and jejunum. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

human_body_nephron_0001.location: How do my kidneys work? Nephron includes glomerulus and tubule
human_body_nephron_0001.claim: What is the kidney unit in which blood is filtered and urine is formed called? Answer: Nephron. It includes a glomerulus and a tubule that returns needed substances to the blood.

mythology_olympus_0001.location: Pantheon paragraph: Mount Olympus, home of gods
mythology_olympus_0001.claim: On which mountain did the Olympian gods live according to ancient Greek myths? Answer: Olympus. This was the gods’ mythical home; Zeus headed the Olympian pantheon. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

mythology_poseidon_0001.location: Zeus paragraph: brothers Hades and Poseidon, their domains
mythology_poseidon_0001.claim: Who was the god of the sea in ancient Greek mythology? Answer: Poseidon. In the myths, his brothers Zeus and Hades ruled the sky and Underworld.

mythology_artemis_0001.location: Apollo paragraph: Artemis, hunting, bow and quiver
mythology_artemis_0001.claim: Which ancient Greek goddess was a patron of hunting? Answer: Artemis. She was often shown with a bow and quiver; Apollo was her twin brother.

mythology_mjolnir_0001.claim: What kind of weapon was Mjölnir in Norse mythology? Answer: Hammer. It belonged to Thor, who fought giants.

mythology_hermes_0001.location: Apollo paragraph: Hermes, winged sandals and herald’s staff
mythology_hermes_0001.claim: Which god served as a messenger in ancient Greek myths? Answer: Hermes. His attributes include winged sandals and a herald’s staff.

mythology_dionysos_0001.location: Other important deities: Dionysos, wine and theater
mythology_dionysos_0001.claim: Which ancient Greek god is associated with wine and theater? Answer: Dionysos. His worship connected winemaking, festivals and theatrical performances.

mythology_odin_ravens_0001.location: Oden har flera djur: two ravens Hugin och Munin report what they saw
mythology_odin_ravens_0001.claim: What birds were Huginn and Muninn, Odin’s companions? Answer: Ravens. In the myths, they flew around the world and reported what they saw to Odin.

mythology_anubis_0001.location: Anubis: black head of a jackal; cemeteries and embalming
mythology_anubis_0001.claim: With the head of which animal was the ancient Egyptian Anubis commonly depicted? Answer: Jackal. He was associated with embalming and the protection of graves.

mythology_athena_bird_0001.location: Wise Athena paragraph: owl, olive tree, weaving and carpentry
mythology_athena_bird_0001.claim: Which bird was sacred to Athena in ancient Greek tradition? Answer: Owl. The goddess was also associated with the olive tree, weaving and crafts.

mythology_thoth_0001.location: Thoth: patron of scribes; ibis or baboon; art of writing
mythology_thoth_0001.claim: Which ancient Egyptian god was a patron of scribes? Answer: Thoth. He was depicted as an ibis or baboon and associated with writing and knowledge.

ancient_world_cuneiform_0001.location: Clay medium; wedge-shaped signs; Latin cuneus
ancient_world_cuneiform_0001.claim: Which ancient writing system takes its name from wedge-shaped signs? Answer: Cuneiform. In Mesopotamia, such signs were impressed into soft clay with a reed or wooden stylus. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

ancient_world_khufu_0001.location: Old Kingdom: Snefru, founder of Fourth Dynasty; Khufu and Great Pyramid
ancient_world_khufu_0001.claim: For which pharaoh was the Great Pyramid at Giza built? Answer: Khufu (Cheops). It belongs to the Old Kingdom and the Fourth Dynasty.

ancient_world_vesuvius_0001.location: Description: Vesuvius, AD 79, Pompei and Herculaneum; day/month deliberately omitted
ancient_world_vesuvius_0001.claim: Which volcano buried Pompeii under volcanic material in AD 79? Answer: Vesuvius. The eruption also struck Herculaneum; buried buildings preserved evidence of Roman life.

ancient_world_papyrus_0001.location: Writing surface: strips of pith from stalk, layered and dried under pressure
ancient_world_papyrus_0001.claim: What did ancient Egyptians use to make papyrus writing sheets? Answer: The pith of plant stalks. Strips were laid in layers and dried under pressure.

ancient_world_upper_egypt_0001.location: Predynastic – Early Dynastic Period: Delta (Lower Egypt), south (Upper Egypt)
ancient_world_upper_egypt_0001.claim: In which direction from Lower Egypt was Upper Egypt located? Answer: South. Lower Egypt corresponded to the Nile Delta, while Upper Egypt lay in the southern valley. Adaptation: Global-MMLU, Cohere Labs et al., Apache 2.0.

ancient_world_qin_emperor_0001.location: Description and criterion (vi): Qin Shi Huang, first unification in 221 BCE
ancient_world_qin_emperor_0001.claim: The famous Terracotta Army belongs to the burial complex of which ruler? Answer: Qin Shi Huang. He was the first emperor of the unified Qin state; unification is dated to 221 BC.

ancient_world_parthenon_deity_0001.location: The Parthenon: temple of Athena Parthenos; gold-and-ivory statue by Pheidias
ancient_world_parthenon_deity_0001.claim: To which goddess was the Parthenon in Athens dedicated? Answer: Athena. The main chamber held Pheidias’s gold-and-ivory statue of the goddess.

ancient_world_rosetta_scholar_0001.location: The Rosetta Stone: Champollion deciphered hieroglyphs in 1822
ancient_world_rosetta_scholar_0001.claim: Who deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs in 1822 using the Rosetta Stone? Answer: Jean-François Champollion. Comparing the inscriptions on the stone provided a key to reading ancient Egyptian texts.

ancient_world_colosseum_opening_0001.location: Opening paragraph: Titus, June–September 80 AD, 100 days; read via direct HTTPS after web timeout
ancient_world_colosseum_opening_0001.claim: In which year AD did Titus hold games to mark the opening of the Colosseum? Answer: 80. The celebrations marking the amphitheater’s opening lasted one hundred days.

ancient_world_terracotta_discovery_0001.location: Description: archaeological discovery in 1974; statues, horses and chariots
ancient_world_terracotta_discovery_0001.claim: In which year was the Terracotta Army at the first Qin emperor’s mausoleum discovered? Answer: 1974. The sculptures depict warriors, horses and chariots in the burial complex.
